key_insight: A structure-preserving augmented Lagrangian FEM can enforce cavitation complementarity exactly in Reynolds and Stokes lubrication models, with the augmentation parameter effectively eliminated from the discrete method.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a reliable way to predict cavitation and pressure in lubricated flows, which is important for design and analysis of bearings and other thin-film lubrication systems.
method: Mixed piecewise-linear FEM for the Reynolds equation with nodal quadrature to satisfy discrete complementarity exactly.
Jump-stabilized Crouzeix-Raviart velocity with piecewise-constant pressure for Stokes flow, using the deviatoric stress formulation.
A computable stability threshold is derived for a multiplier-free stabilized alternative.
evidence_signal: The paper reports classical first-order error estimates and numerical examples that verify well-posedness, stability, and the sensitivity of cavitation predictions to model end conditions.
watch_item: Pressure agreement alone may be misleading: close pressure profiles in Reynolds and Stokes models do not necessarily imply similar cavity predictions, and results can depend strongly on boundary/end conditions.
paper_title: Structure-Preserving Augmented Lagrangian Finite Element Methods for Cavitation in Reynolds and Stokes Flows
